name: COrPO (やさしいスイーツカフェ COrPO)

claims.text: Dedicated gluten-free specialty shop: 「小麦を使用しない、全てグルテンフリーの商品を提供しております」— no wheat is used and all products are gluten-free; outside food is banned except certified wheat-free baby food.
Rice-flour bread is 100% 米粉 with 「小麦粉一切不使用」 (no wheat flour whatsoever).
All lunch seasonings are stated to be gluten-free (「調味料もすべてグルテンフリー」-style claim), consistent with the shop's wheat-free premises.
Positioned explicitly for people with wheat/flour allergy and gut-health goals; the whole operation is wheat-free by design.
Entire menu — breads, lunches, sweets — is gluten-free; wheat flour is neither used nor brought onto the premises.
Uses no wheat flour and no refined white sugar, with organic-leaning sourcing.

Venue's own claim: 「店内の全てのメニューが小麦・卵・乳製品不使用…調理器具も完全に分けており、小麦粉の持ち込みは一切禁止」 — every menu item is wheat/egg/dairy-free, utensils are completely separated, and no wheat flour may be brought onto the premises.
The entire cafe uses no wheat flour (卵・牛乳・小麦粉を使用しない野菜カフェ); bread is made from rice flour (米粉パン), so there is no in-house wheat baking to cross-contaminate.
Japanese reviewers note that food not compliant with the cafe's allergen policy may not be brought into the shop (アレルギー対応でない食品の持ち込みは禁止).
The whole menu is declared wheat-free, which implies any soy-based seasoning is a wheat-free type (tamari); this was not explicitly documented, so celiacs should confirm on the day.
Cafe is egg- and dairy-free throughout and all sweets are vegan, but some dishes may contain fish, so vegans should request a plant-based version.
Owner Chiaki has managed food allergies since childhood; the shop is built around allergen-free (卵・牛乳・小麦不使用) cooking.
Reviewers advise contacting the cafe in advance if you have specific allergy or ingredient concerns (アレルギーや食材が気になる方は事前に問い合わせを).
100% wheat-free kitchen with separated utensils and a ban on wheat flour entering the premises — very low celiac cross-contact risk.
Owner has lifelong personal experience of food allergies, so allergen handling is a core focus.
Kids' plate excludes the 27 major allergens, indicating serious allergen-management practice.

Shop is a 100% rice-flour operation with no wheat flour on premises (完全グルテンフリー専門店), minimizing airborne/flour cross-contact; no explicit dedicated-kitchen protocol or celiac audit is published, so confirm CC handling on visit.
A bakery — no soy sauce central to products; the shop states it uses no wheat, egg, dairy or soy at all in its core line.
Core line avoids egg/dairy/soy, but some sweet items add butter or cream cheese, so animal-ingredient contact varies by product.
No documented allergen-handling protocol found in available sources; recommend confirming directly.
Uses 100% self-grown rice flour and declares no wheat, egg, dairy or soy — a genuinely wheat-free bakery.

name: Kashiya Fujinomiya (菓子屋 藤ノ宮)

claims.text: Company states the entire factory switched to fully wheat-free production in summer 2022: 「完全に小麦を使わないグルテンフリー食品製造を行うことにいたしました」 — no wheat product line remains on premises, so cross-contact risk is very low.

The factory used shared confectionery/senbei equipment before the 2022 wheat wind-down; no separate certification or explicit allergen-testing protocol is published, so extremely sensitive celiacs may confirm the equipment cleaning history.
Sweets/bakery only; no soy-sauce-based dishes served. Sweets use white-bean paste (白あん) and rice flour, not soy sauce.
Egg is used in the 栗せん and 白あん cakes and is handled in the same kitchen, so shared equipment may contact egg; the plain rice-flour bread appears egg/dairy-free but is produced in the same facility.
The shop is expressly built around wheat-free customers (celiac / wheat allergy) and its whole raison d'être is gluten-free confectionery, indicating high staff awareness of wheat avoidance.
Curated Japanese celiac guide empacede rates it グルテンフリー ★★★★★, describing it as carrying no wheat products with no cross-contamination risk.
100% rice-flour bread and a legacy wheat-free senbei; the entire premises is dedicated to gluten-free output.
100% rice-flour bakery with no wheat used anywhere; the venue states 「小麦・卵・乳不使用、米粉を100%使用したグルテンフリーのパン」, so cross-contact from wheat is not a factor on the premises.
Cafe menu is entirely wheat/egg/dairy-free: 「メニューはもちろん全てが"グルテンフリー" 小麦・卵・乳不使用のランチ」.
Lunch plates are declared wheat-free, implying no standard (wheat-based) soy sauce is used; confirm the seasoning on the day if highly sensitive.
All items are egg- and dairy-free by policy, reducing vegan cross-contact concerns; meat may appear in some lunch/bagel items.
Owner is a registered dietitian who develops products with individual allergy responses in mind.
Dedicated wheat/egg/dairy-free facility — nothing containing wheat is made or sold on site.
Aichi's first rice-flour bagel specialist, run by a registered dietitian using domestic rice flour.

name: Komeko no Mise Palette (こめこの店Palette)

claims.text: Venue states 「製造施設内への小麦の持ち込みは完全禁止、米粉パン専用の設備・器具のみを使用し、コンタミネーション（混入）リスクはゼロ」 — wheat completely banned from the facility, rice-bread-only equipment, zero contamination risk.
MAFF Tokai regional 米粉店 mapping and Tabelog list it as a rice-flour/gluten-free specialist.
As a wheat-free facility, savory items (gyoza/shumai) avoid wheat-based components; confirm the dipping sauce/seasoning is tamari-based or wheat-free if highly sensitive.
Bagels/breads use only plant ingredients (rice flour, natural yeast, salt, kibi sugar, rice oil); meat appears in gyoza/shumai lunch items.
Whole-facility wheat ban reflects an allergy-first operation aimed at children and the wheat-sensitive.
Explicit zero-contamination claim: wheat banned from the facility, rice-only equipment.
Additive-free bagels from 100% domestic rice flour, natural yeast, natural salt, kibi sugar and rice oil.
The entire shop uses no wheat flour whatsoever, so cross-contact with wheat is inherently minimal; however, no formal celiac cross-contamination protocol is published.
Butter, fresh cream, cheese and eggs are used throughout; not a vegan-oriented kitchen.
Press reports the shop serves customers with wheat allergies and emphasizes body-friendly ingredients (minimal colorants/preservatives), but published allergen-handling detail is limited.
100% wheat-free kitchen using 8+ gluten-free flours (rice, white sorghum, tapioca, kudzu, brown rice).
Opened 2017 as a dedicated gluten-free sweets specialist; every product is gluten-free.
No grain products (wheat, barley, rye, oats) are permitted to enter the premises at all, eliminating the primary cross-contamination vector.
All kitchen equipment was purchased new rather than leased, ensuring no residual gluten from prior use.
Staff uniforms are washed exclusively on-site to prevent outside gluten introduction.
Gluten-free soy sauce and miso are specifically sourced; standard wheat-containing soy sauce and miso are not used in any preparation.
The kitchen is not vegan-dedicated. Bento boxes regularly contain fish, chicken, and eggs; plant-based sides are prepared in the same kitchen environment.
The shop advises contacting them directly for allergen accommodation requests beyond gluten: 「食物アレルギー対応につきましてはお問い合わせください」(Please inquire about food allergy accommodations).
Protocols account for even trace-protein quantities sufficient to trigger allergic reactions, reflecting the founder's personal experience with wheat allergy.
Tokai region's first dedicated gluten-free bento shop — the entire menu is safe for wheat allergy; no need to ask or modify orders.
The founder is herself a wheat-allergy sufferer and certified gluten-free advisor, bringing lived-experience credibility to every safety decision.
